translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, at each lecture only the kowtow ceremony was observed.

sentences.zh: 以次上殿，東西序立。

translations.literal: In order they entered the hall and stood in ranks east and west.
translations.idiomatic: They entered the hall in succession and stood in ranks to the east and west.

sentences.zh: 序班二員，舉御案於座前，二員舉講案置御案南正中。

translations.literal: Two ushers raised the imperial lectern before the throne; two ushers raised the lecture lectern and placed it directly south of the imperial lectern.
translations.idiomatic: Two ushers carried the imperial lectern before the throne; two others carried the lecture lectern and set it directly south of the imperial lectern.

sentences.zh: 鴻臚官贊進講。

translations.literal: An official of the Court of State Ceremonial announced the advance to lecture.
translations.idiomatic: A Court of State Ceremonial official announced the commencement of the lecture.

sentences.zh: 講官二員從東西班出，詣講案前，北向並立。

translations.literal: Two lecturers came forth from the eastern and western ranks, proceeded before the lecture lectern, and stood side by side facing north.
translations.idiomatic: Two lecturers stepped forward from the eastern and western ranks, proceeded to the lecture lectern, and stood side by side facing north.

sentences.zh: 東西展書官各至御案南銅鶴下，相向立。

translations.literal: The eastern and western book-unfolding officials each came to beneath the bronze cranes south of the imperial lectern and stood facing one another.
translations.idiomatic: The book-unfolding officials from the east and west each took position beneath the bronze cranes south of the imperial lectern and stood facing each other.

sentences.zh: 鴻臚官贊講拜，興。

translations.literal: The Court of State Ceremonial official announced the lecturers' bow; they rose.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of State Ceremonial official announced the lecturers' bow, and they rose.

sentences.zh: 東班展書官詣御案前，跪展《四書》，退立於東鶴下。

translations.literal: The eastern-rank book-unfolding official proceeded before the imperial lectern, knelt and unfolded the Four Books, withdrew and stood beneath the eastern crane.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern book-unfolding official approached the imperial lectern, knelt to unfold the Four Books, then withdrew to stand beneath the eastern crane.

sentences.zh: 講官至講案前立，奏講某書，講畢退。

translations.literal: The lecturer stood before the lecture lectern, reported which book would be lectured upon, lectured to completion, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The lecturer stood before the lecture lectern, announced which text would be lectured upon, delivered the lecture, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 展書官跪掩書，仍退立鶴下。

translations.literal: The book-unfolding official knelt to close the book, then again withdrew and stood beneath the crane.
translations.idiomatic: The book-unfolding official knelt to close the book, then withdrew again to stand beneath the crane.

sentences.zh: 西班展書官展經或史，講官進講，退，如初。

translations.literal: The western-rank book-unfolding official unfolded a classic or history; the lecturer advanced to lecture, withdrew, and the procedure was as before.
translations.idiomatic: The western book-unfolding official unfolded a classic or history; the lecturer delivered the lecture and withdrew, following the same procedure as before.

sentences.zh: 鴻臚官贊講官拜，興。

translations.literal: The Court of State Ceremonial official announced the lecturers' bow; they rose.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of State Ceremonial official announced the lecturers' bow, and they rose.

sentences.zh: 各退就東西班，展書官隨之，序班徹御案講案。

translations.literal: Each withdrew to the eastern and western ranks; the book-unfolding officials followed; the ushers removed the imperial and lecture lecterns.
translations.idiomatic: All withdrew to the eastern and western ranks, the book-unfolding officials following; the ushers removed the imperial and lecture lecterns.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，命賜酒飯。

translations.literal: When the rites were complete, the emperor ordered wine and food to be granted.
translations.idiomatic: When the ceremony was complete, the emperor ordered wine and a meal to be granted.

sentences.zh: 各官出至丹陛，行叩頭禮。

translations.literal: The officials went out to the vermillion steps and performed the kowtow rite.
translations.idiomatic: The officials proceeded to the vermillion steps and performed the kowtow ceremony.

sentences.zh: 至左順門，酒飯畢，入行叩頭禮。

translations.literal: At the Left Gate of Compliance, when the wine and food were finished, they performed the kowtow rite.
translations.idiomatic: At the Left Gate of Compliance, after the wine and meal were finished, they performed the kowtow ceremony.

sentences.zh: 隆慶元年，定先一日告奉先殿，告几筵。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longqing it was fixed that on the preceding day announcement would be made at the Hall of Ancestors Venerated and at the spirit tablets.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Longqing it was decreed that on the day before, announcement would be made at the Hall of Ancestors Venerated and before the spirit tablets.

sentences.zh: 是日，帝詣文華殿左室，展禮先聖先師。

translations.literal: On that day the emperor proceeded to the left chamber of the Hall of Literary Glory and performed rites to the previous sages and previous teachers.
translations.idiomatic: On that day the emperor went to the left chamber of the Hall of Literary Glory and performed rites to the prior sages and teachers.

sentences.zh: 講章於前兩日先進呈覽。

translations.literal: The lecture chapters were submitted two days in advance for inspection.
translations.idiomatic: The lecture chapters were submitted two days in advance for the emperor's review.

sentences.zh: 萬曆二年，定春講以二月十二日起，至五月初二日止，秋講以八月十二日起，至十月初二日止，不必題請。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wanli it was fixed that spring lectures began on the twelfth day of the second month and ended on the second day of the fifth month, and autumn lectures began on the twelfth day of the eighth month and ended on the second day of the tenth month, with no need to memorialize requesting permission.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Wanli it was decreed that spring lectures ran from the twelfth day of the second month to the second day of the fifth month, and autumn lectures from the twelfth day of the eighth month to the second day of the tenth month, with no need to memorialize for permission.

sentences.zh: 日講，御文華穿殿，止用講讀官內閣學士侍班，不用侍儀等官。

translations.literal: For daily lectures, the emperor presided in the connecting hall of the Hall of Literary Glory; only lecturers, readers, and Grand Secretaries attended in the roster, without ceremony-attending officials and the like.
translations.idiomatic: For daily lectures, the emperor presided in the connecting hall of the Hall of Literary Glory; only the lecturers, readers, and Grand Secretaries served on the attendance roster, without ceremony-attending officials or the like.

sentences.zh: 講官或四或六。

translations.literal: Lecturers numbered either four or six.
translations.idiomatic: There were either four or six lecturers.

sentences.zh: 開讀初，吉服，五拜三叩首，後常服，一拜三叩首。

translations.literal: At the initial opening of reading, in auspicious dress: five bows and three kowtows; thereafter in ordinary dress: one bow and three kowtows.
translations.idiomatic: At the first session of reading, the emperor wore ceremonial dress and performed five bows and three kowtows; thereafter in ordinary dress he performed one bow and three kowtows.

sentences.zh: 閣臣同侍於殿內，候帝口宣 「先生來」，同進，叩首，東西立。

translations.literal: Grand Secretaries attended together within the hall; waiting until the emperor orally proclaimed "The teachers have come," they entered together, kowtowed, and stood east and west.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretaries attended together within the hall; when the emperor orally proclaimed "Let the teachers enter," they entered together, kowtowed, and stood to the east and west.

sentences.zh: 讀者先至御前一揖，至案展書，壓金尺，執牙籤。

translations.literal: The reader first came before the emperor and made one bow, went to the lectern to unfold the book, pressed it with a gold ruler, and held an ivory bookmark.
translations.idiomatic: The reader first approached the emperor and bowed once, then went to the lectern to unfold the book, weighting it with a gold ruler and holding an ivory bookmark.

sentences.zh: 讀五過，掩書一揖退。

translations.literal: He read five passes through, closed the book, made one bow, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He read through the passage five times, closed the book, bowed once, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 先書，次經，次史，進講如讀儀。

translations.literal: First the book, then the classic, then the history; advancing to lecture followed the reading rite.
translations.idiomatic: The sequence was first the book, then the classic, then the history; the lecture followed the same procedure as the reading.

sentences.zh: 侍書官侍習書畢，各叩頭退。

translations.literal: Attending scribe officials attended while calligraphy practice was completed; each kowtowed and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Attending scribe officials supervised calligraphy practice; when it was complete, each kowtowed and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 於文華殿賜茶，文華門賜酒飯。

translations.literal: Tea was granted in the Hall of Literary Glory; wine and food were granted at the Gate of Literary Glory.
translations.idiomatic: Tea was served in the Hall of Literary Glory, and wine and a meal at the Gate of Literary Glory.

sentences.zh: 午講，隆慶六年定。

translations.literal: The afternoon lecture was fixed in the sixth year of Longqing.
translations.idiomatic: The afternoon lecture was established in the sixth year of Longqing.

sentences.zh: 每日早講畢，帝進暖閣少憩，閱章奏。

translations.literal: Each day after the morning lecture was complete, the emperor entered the warm pavilion to rest briefly and review memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Each day after the morning lecture, the emperor retired to the warm pavilion for a brief rest and to review memorials.

sentences.zh: 閣臣等退西廂房，久之，率講官再進午講，講《通鑑節要》及《貞觀政要》。

translations.literal: Grand Secretaries and the like withdrew to the western side chamber; after some time they led the lecturers to enter again for the afternoon lecture, lecturing on Essentials from the Comprehensive Mirror and Essentials of Governance in the Zhenguan Era.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Secretaries withdrew to the western side chamber; after some time they led the lecturers back for the afternoon session, lecturing on Essentials from the Comprehensive Mirror and Essentials of Governance in the Zhenguan Era.

sentences.zh: 講畢，帝還宮。

translations.literal: When the lecture was complete, the emperor returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the lecture was finished, the emperor returned to the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 凡三、六、九視朝日，暫免講讀。

translations.literal: On all court-audience days of the third, sixth, and ninth, lectures and reading were temporarily omitted.
translations.idiomatic: On the third, sixth, and ninth days when the emperor held court audience, lectures and reading were temporarily suspended.

sentences.zh: 又嘉靖六年定制，月三、八日，經筵日講官二員，講《大學衍義》。

translations.literal: Furthermore, regulations fixed in the sixth year of Jiajing: on the third and eighth days of each month, two Classics Lectern daily lecturers lectured on Elaboration of the Meaning of the Great Learning.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations established in the sixth year of Jiajing further specified that on the third and eighth of each month, two Classics Lectern daily lecturers would lecture on Elaboration of the Meaning of the Great Learning.

sentences.zh: 十年，定無逸殿講儀。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, lecture rites for the Hall of Non-Indulgence were fixed.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, the lecture ceremony for the Hall of Non-Indulgence was established.

sentences.zh: 質明，帝常服乘輦至殿門，衆官於門外迎候。

translations.literal: At daybreak the emperor in ordinary dress rode the palanquin to the hall gate; the multitude of officials awaited to welcome him outside the gate.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak the emperor, in ordinary dress, rode the palanquin to the hall gate, where officials awaited him outside.

sentences.zh: 帝降輦，乘板輿，至殿升座。

translations.literal: The emperor descended from the palanquin, rode a board litter, entered the hall and ascended the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor descended from the palanquin, was carried on a board litter into the hall, and took his seat.

sentences.zh: 各官於殿門外一拜三叩首，入內，東西序立。

translations.literal: Each official outside the hall gate performed one bow and three kowtows, entered within, and stood in ranks east and west.
translations.idiomatic: Each official performed one bow and three kowtows outside the hall gate, then entered and stood in ranks to the east and west.

sentences.zh: 贊進講，講官大學士一員出班叩首。

translations.literal: When the advance to lecture was announced, one Grand Secretary lecturer came forth from the ranks and kowtowed.
translations.idiomatic: When the lecture was announced, one lecturing Grand Secretary stepped forward from the ranks and kowtowed.

sentences.zh: 命賜坐，一叩首，乃坐。

translations.literal: On being ordered to be granted a seat, he kowtowed once, then sat.
translations.idiomatic: On being granted permission to sit, he kowtowed once and then took his seat.

sentences.zh: 講畢，展書官跪掩講章，講官叩頭復班。

translations.literal: When the lecture was complete, the book-unfolding official knelt to close the lecture chapter; the lecturer kowtowed and returned to the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: When the lecture was finished, the book-unfolding official knelt to close the lecture text; the lecturer kowtowed and returned to his place in the ranks.

sentences.zh: 又學士一員承旨坐講，如初禮畢。

translations.literal: Again one academician, receiving the imperial command, sat to lecture; when complete the rites were as at first.
translations.idiomatic: Then another academician, receiving the imperial command, sat to deliver a lecture; when finished, the ceremony concluded as before.

sentences.zh: 各官至豳風亭候駕至，亭內賜宴。

translations.literal: Each official went to the Bin Wind Pavilion to await the imperial progress; within the pavilion a banquet was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The officials proceeded to the Bin Wind Pavilion to await the emperor's arrival, and a banquet was served within the pavilion.

sentences.zh: 東宮出閣講學儀

translations.literal: Rites for the Eastern Palace's Emergence from Seclusion for Study
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Palace Emergence-from-Seclusion Study Rites

sentences.zh: 太祖命學士宋濂授皇太子、諸王經於大本堂，後於文華後殿。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor ordered Academician Song Lian to teach the classics to the crown prince and the princes in the Hall of the Great Foundation; later this was moved to the rear hall of the Hall of Literary Glory.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor ordered Academician Song Lian to instruct the crown prince and the princes in the classics at the Hall of the Great Foundation; later instruction moved to the rear hall of the Hall of Literary Glory.

sentences.zh: 世宗改爲便殿，遂移殿東廂。

translations.literal: The Jiajing Emperor changed it to a convenience hall, and it was then moved to the eastern side chamber of the hall.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiajing Emperor converted it to a convenience hall, and instruction was moved to the hall's eastern side chamber.

sentences.zh: 天順二年，定出閣儀。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianshun, emergence-from-seclusion rites were fixed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianshun, the emergence-from-seclusion ceremony was established.

sentences.zh: 是日早，侍衛侍儀如常。

translations.literal: Early on that day, guard attendants and ceremony attendants were as usual.
translations.idiomatic: That morning, guard and ceremony attendants were deployed as usual.

sentences.zh: 執事官於文華後殿四拜，鴻臚官請皇太子升殿，師保等於丹陛上四拜。

translations.literal: Presiding officials performed four bows in the rear hall of the Hall of Literary Glory; a Court of State Ceremonial official requested the crown prince to ascend the hall; tutors and guardians and the like performed four bows on the vermillion steps.
translations.idiomatic: Presiding officials performed four bows in the rear hall of the Hall of Literary Glory; a Court of State Ceremonial official invited the crown prince to ascend the hall; tutors, guardians, and their colleagues performed four bows on the vermillion steps.

sentences.zh: 各官退出，內侍導皇太子至後殿升座，以書案進。

translations.literal: The officials withdrew; palace attendants guided the crown prince to the rear hall to ascend the throne, and the book lectern was brought forward.
translations.idiomatic: The officials withdrew; palace attendants escorted the crown prince to the rear hall to take his seat, and the book lectern was brought forward.

sentences.zh: 侍班侍讀講官入，分班東西立。

translations.literal: Attendance-roster, reading, and lecturing officials entered and stood in ranks east and west.
translations.idiomatic: Officials on the attendance roster together with the reading and lecturing instructors entered and stood in ranks to the east and west.

sentences.zh: 內侍展書，侍讀講官以次進讀講，叩頭而退。

translations.literal: Palace attendants unfolded the books; reading and lecturing officials in succession advanced to read and lecture, kowtowed, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendants unfolded the books; the reading and lecturing instructors successively advanced to read and lecture, then kowtowed and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 其每日講讀儀，早朝退後，皇太子出閣升座，不用侍衛等官，惟侍班侍讀講官入，行叩頭禮。

translations.literal: As for the daily reading and lecture rites: after the morning audience was dismissed, the crown prince emerged from seclusion and ascended the throne; guard attendants and the like were not used; only attendance-roster, reading, and lecturing officials entered and performed the kowtow rite.
translations.idiomatic: For the daily reading and lecture ceremony: after the morning audience, the crown prince emerged from seclusion and took his seat; guard attendants were dispensed with; only attendance-roster, reading, and lecturing officials entered and performed the kowtow ceremony.

sentences.zh: 內侍展書，先讀《四書》，則東班侍讀官向前，伴讀十數遍，退復班。

translations.literal: Palace attendants unfolded the books; when the Four Books were read first, the eastern-rank reading official came forward, accompanied the reading for more than ten passes, withdrew and returned to the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendants unfolded the books; when the Four Books were read first, the eastern reading instructor stepped forward and accompanied the reading for more than ten repetitions, then withdrew to his place in the ranks.

sentences.zh: 次讀經或史，則西班伴讀，亦如之。

translations.literal: Next, when a classic or history was read, the western rank accompanied the reading, likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Next, when a classic or history was read, the western instructor accompanied the reading in the same manner.

sentences.zh: 讀畢，各官退。

translations.literal: When reading was complete, each official withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When reading was finished, the officials withdrew.

sentences.zh: 至巳時，各官入，內侍展書，侍講官講早所讀《四書》畢，退班。

translations.literal: At the si hour each official entered; palace attendants unfolded the books; the lecturing official lectured on the Four Books read that morning to completion, and withdrew from the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: At the si hour the officials entered; palace attendants unfolded the books; the lecturing instructor delivered the morning's lecture on the Four Books, then withdrew from the ranks.

sentences.zh: 次講經史亦然。

translations.literal: Next, lecturing on classics and histories was likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Lectures on the classics and histories followed the same procedure.

sentences.zh: 講畢，侍書官侍習寫字。

translations.literal: When lecture was complete, attending scribe officials attended while writing characters was practiced.
translations.idiomatic: When the lecture was finished, attending scribe officials supervised calligraphy practice.

sentences.zh: 寫畢，各官叩頭退。

translations.literal: When writing was complete, each official kowtowed and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When calligraphy practice was complete, each official kowtowed and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 凡讀書，三日後一溫，背誦成熟。

translations.literal: Generally in reading books, after three days there was one review, reciting from memory until fluent.
translations.idiomatic: In general, after three days of reading came one review session, with recitation from memory until the text was mastered.

sentences.zh: 溫書之日，不授新書。

translations.literal: On days of reviewing books, no new books were assigned.
translations.idiomatic: On review days, no new texts were assigned.

sentences.zh: 凡寫字，春夏秋日百字，冬日五十字。

translations.literal: Generally in writing characters, in spring, summer, and autumn one hundred characters; in winter fifty characters.
translations.idiomatic: For calligraphy practice, one hundred characters were assigned in spring, summer, and autumn, and fifty in winter.

sentences.zh: 凡朔望節假及大風雨雪、隆寒盛暑，則暫停。

translations.literal: Generally on new and full moon days, festival holidays, and days of great wind, rain, or snow, extreme cold, or intense heat, practice was temporarily suspended.
translations.idiomatic: On new and full moon days, festival holidays, and days of severe wind, rain, or snow, extreme cold, or intense heat, instruction was temporarily suspended.

sentences.zh: 弘治十一年更定，三師三少並宮僚于丹陛四拜畢，從殿左右門入，東西立。

translations.literal: Re-fixed in the eleventh year of Hongzhi: the Three Tutors, Three Supplements, and palace staff, having completed four bows on the vermillion steps, entered through the left and right gates of the hall and stood east and west.
translations.idiomatic: Revised in the eleventh year of Hongzhi: the Three Tutors, Three Supplements, and palace staff, having completed four bows on the vermillion steps, entered through the hall's side gates and stood to the east and west.

sentences.zh: 候講讀畢，叩頭退。

translations.literal: They waited until reading and lecturing were complete, kowtowed, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: They waited until reading and lecturing were finished, then kowtowed and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 隆慶六年，改設皇太子座於文華殿之東廂，正中西向。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Longqing, the crown prince's seat was moved and set in the eastern side chamber of the Hall of Literary Glory, centrally placed and facing west.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Longqing, the crown prince's seat was relocated to the eastern side chamber of the Hall of Literary Glory, centered and facing west.

sentences.zh: 每日講讀各官，先詣文華門外東西向，序立。

translations.literal: Each day the reading and lecturing officials first proceeded outside the Gate of Literary Glory, faced east and west, and stood in order.
translations.idiomatic: Each day the reading and lecturing officials first assembled outside the Gate of Literary Glory, facing east and west, and stood in order.

sentences.zh: 候帝御日講經筵畢，皇太子出閣升座。

translations.literal: They waited until the emperor had completed presiding at daily lectures and the Classics Lectern; then the crown prince emerged from seclusion and ascended the throne.
translations.idiomatic: They waited until the emperor had finished his daily lectures and Classics Lectern session; then the crown prince emerged from seclusion and took his seat.

sentences.zh: 凡東宮初講時，閣臣連侍五日，後每月三、八日一至，先拜出，然後各官入。

translations.literal: Generally when the Eastern Palace first began lectures, Grand Secretaries attended in succession for five days; thereafter on the third and eighth of each month one would come once, bow first and withdraw, and then the other officials would enter.
translations.idiomatic: When the Eastern Palace first began lectures, Grand Secretaries attended consecutively for five days; thereafter one attended on the third and eighth of each month, bowing and withdrawing first before the other officials entered.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十一年，署禮部事學士顧錫疇言：「東宮嘉禮告成，累朝錫賚有據。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Chongzhen, Academician Gu Xichou, acting head of the Ministry of Rites, said: "The Eastern Palace auspicious rites have been completed; successive reigns have precedents for bestowed rewards.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Chongzhen, Academician Gu Xichou, acting head of the Ministry of Rites, said: "The Eastern Palace auspicious rites have been completed, and successive reigns offer precedents for bestowed rewards.

sentences.zh: 《實錄》載成化十五年，皇太子出閣講學，六卿皆加保、傅。

translations.literal: The Veritable Records record that in the fifteenth year of Chenghua, when the crown prince emerged from seclusion for study, the six chief ministers were all granted titles of guardian and tutor.
translations.idiomatic: The Veritable Records record that in the fifteenth year of Chenghua, when the crown prince emerged from seclusion for study, all six chief ministers were granted guardian and tutor titles.

sentences.zh: 弘治十年，皇太子出閣講學，內閣徐溥等四人、尚書馬文升等七人，俱加宮保。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Hongzhi, when the crown prince emerged from seclusion for study, four from the Inner Cabinet including Xu Pu and seven ministers including Ma Wensheng were all granted palace-guardian titles.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Hongzhi, when the crown prince emerged from seclusion for study, four Inner Cabinet members including Xu Pu and seven ministers including Ma Wensheng were all granted palace-guardian titles.

sentences.zh: 」帝命酌議行之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered that this be considered and deliberated upon for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered that the matter be deliberated and implemented accordingly.

sentences.zh: 諸王讀書儀

translations.literal: Rites for Imperial Princes' Study
translations.idiomatic: Princely Study Rites

sentences.zh: 書堂在皇極門右廂。

translations.literal: The study hall was in the right side chamber of the Gate of Imperial Supremacy.
translations.idiomatic: The study hall was located in the right side chamber of the Gate of Imperial Supremacy.

sentences.zh: 講官選部曹或進士改授翰林官充之。

translations.literal: Lecturers were selected from department officials or jinshi appointees reassigned as Hanlin officials to fill the posts.
translations.idiomatic: Lecturers were drawn from department officials or jinshi degree holders reassigned as Hanlin academicians.

sentences.zh: 天順二年定，初入書堂，其日早，王至右順門之北書堂，面東，中坐。

translations.literal: Fixed in the second year of Tianshun: upon first entering the study hall, early that day the prince came to the study hall north of the Right Gate of Compliance, faced east, and sat centrally.
translations.idiomatic: Established in the second year of Tianshun: upon first entering the study hall, the prince that morning proceeded to the study hall north of the Right Gate of Compliance, faced east, and sat at the center.

sentences.zh: 提督講讀並講讀官行四拜禮。

translations.literal: The superintendent of reading and lecturing together with reading and lecturing officials performed the four-bow rite.
translations.idiomatic: The superintendent of reading and lecturing together with the reading and lecturing instructors performed the four-bow ceremony.

sentences.zh: 內官捧書展於案上，就案左坐。

translations.literal: Palace eunuchs held out the book and unfolded it on the lectern; the prince sat to the left of the lectern.
translations.idiomatic: Palace eunuchs unfolded the book on the lectern, and the prince sat to the left of it.

sentences.zh: 講讀官進立於案右。

translations.literal: Reading and lecturing officials advanced and stood to the right of the lectern.
translations.idiomatic: The reading and lecturing instructors stepped forward and stood to the right of the lectern.

sentences.zh: 伴讀十遍，叩頭退。

translations.literal: They accompanied the reading for ten passes, kowtowed, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: They accompanied the reading for ten repetitions, then kowtowed and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 每日講讀，清晨，王至書堂，講讀官行叩頭禮，伴讀十遍，出。

translations.literal: For daily reading and lecturing, early in the morning the prince came to the study hall; reading and lecturing officials performed the kowtow rite, accompanied reading for ten passes, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: For daily reading and lecturing, each morning the prince came to the study hall; the reading and lecturing instructors performed the kowtow ceremony, accompanied the reading for ten repetitions, and departed.

sentences.zh: 飯後，復詣堂伴看寫字。

translations.literal: After the meal, they again proceeded to the hall to accompany and observe writing characters.
translations.idiomatic: After the meal, they returned to the hall to supervise calligraphy practice.

sentences.zh: 講書畢，仍叩頭退。

translations.literal: When lecturing on the book was complete, they again kowtowed and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the lecture was finished, they again kowtowed and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 萬曆六年定，書堂設中座，書案在左，寫字案在右。

translations.literal: Fixed in the sixth year of Wanli: the study hall had a central seat, the book lectern to the left, and the writing-character lectern to the right.
translations.idiomatic: Established in the sixth year of Wanli: the study hall was arranged with a central seat, the book lectern to the left, and the calligraphy lectern to the right.

sentences.zh: 輔臣率講讀侍書官候於門外。

translations.literal: Assisting ministers led reading, lecturing, and attending scribe officials to wait outside the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Assisting ministers led the reading, lecturing, and scribe instructors to wait outside the gate.

sentences.zh: 王入書堂，傳令旨「先生進」。

translations.literal: The prince entered the study hall; the imperial command was transmitted: "Let the teachers enter."
translations.idiomatic: The prince entered the study hall and transmitted the command: "Let the teachers enter."

sentences.zh: 輔臣率各官入，四拜，分班侍立。

translations.literal: Assisting ministers led the various officials to enter, performed four bows, and stood in attendance by ranks.
translations.idiomatic: The assisting ministers led the instructors in, they performed four bows, and stood in attendance by rank.

sentences.zh: 講讀官以次授書各十遍訖，令旨「先生吃酒飯」，各官出，王暫入堂南間少憩。

translations.literal: Reading and lecturing officials in succession taught the books, each for ten passes to completion; the command was transmitted: "Teachers, take wine and food"; the officials went out; the prince briefly entered the southern chamber of the hall to rest.
translations.idiomatic: The reading and lecturing instructors successively conducted instruction, ten repetitions for each text; the command was given: "Teachers, take your meal"; the officials withdrew, and the prince briefly retired to the southern chamber of the hall.

sentences.zh: 輔臣各率官入。

translations.literal: Each assisting minister led the officials to enter.
translations.idiomatic: Each assisting minister led his instructors back in.

sentences.zh: 令旨「先生進」，遂入分班侍立。

translations.literal: The command "Let the teachers enter" was given; they then entered and stood in attendance by ranks.
translations.idiomatic: On the command "Let the teachers enter," they entered and stood in attendance by rank.

sentences.zh: 侍書官看寫字，講讀以次進講畢，各官一拜出。

translations.literal: Attending scribe officials observed writing characters; reading and lecturing officials in succession advanced to lecture to completion; each official performed one bow and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Scribe instructors supervised calligraphy practice; the reading and lecturing instructors successively delivered their lectures; each official bowed once and departed.
